I will do it the way I have been doing on this land, with a little care on the money. For wheat and maize, I use the same 10.1 mu because one follows the other. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard, because if yield falls, that hurts more than spending a bit extra. I look at what people around me do, and if I am not sure, I stay close to the old way. Since I have well water, I will use irrigation when the crop really needs it. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put a solid base fertilizer, water a few times, and spray a couple of times if I see disease or bugs. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, give enough nitrogen because maize eats fertilizer, water in key times, and spray a couple of times. On 10.1 mu with only 2 people in the house, I will keep the work simple and use rotary tillage, because it saves labor and still works fine on our fields.
